GIG Mobility Group has announced plans to expand its operations beyond interstate passenger transportation by investing in digital platforms that connect vehicle hire, travel bookings and other mobility services. The company said the expansion was part of a strategy to diversify its business, improve customer convenience and strengthen its presence in Nigeria’s transportation market. The Chief Executive Officer of GIGM, Dr Enahoro Okhae, disclosed this on Wednesday during the Abuja launch of PASS by GIGM and hireX by GIGM, two platforms designed to broaden the company’s transportation services. Okhae said, “We have chosen to grow, to build, to innovate and to lead, and that is why we have decided to create what we call Integrato, an ecosystem rather than just moving people.” He explained that the company was moving away from its traditional identity as an interstate transport operator towards a broader mobility business integrating transportation, travel and lifestyle services. According to the company, hireX is a vehicle hire marketplace that allows customers to book vehicles with professional drivers for airport transfers, corporate travel, events and journeys within Abuja. The launch also featured PASS, another platform within the company’s expanding mobility operations. Okhae said changing customer expectations, particularly the demand for faster services, digital access and convenient travel arrangements, informed the company’s decision to diversify. They expect digital access. Customers want a seamless experience.” He disclosed that GIGM had also expanded its physical operations, opening a terminal in Gwagwalada, Abuja, on Tuesday, bringing its network to 40 terminals across West Africa. The new facility adds to the company’s presence in Utako, Zuba, Mararaba and Madalla, reflecting its efforts to reach more passengers within the Federal Capital Territory. Speaking on the technology behind the expansion, GIGM’s Head of Product, Charles Oloyede, said digital systems had enabled the company to manage increasingly complex transportation operations and develop services beyond road travel. 2027: Obasanjo’s son backs Tinubu’s re-election Tinubu returns to Abuja after pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia 2027: Obasanjo’s son backs Tinubu’s re-election “But we rely on technology because without that, there is a limit to what you can do,” he said. Oloyede explained that the company’s technology infrastructure supported coordination across its operations, reducing dependence on manual processes and improving service delivery. He added that the company was developing digital solutions for different aspects of mobility, including road and air travel, while extending services previously available in Lagos to Abuja. Meanwhile, the Director-General of the National Automotive Design and Development Council, Oluwemimo Osanipin, stressed that technology-driven transportation businesses must address concerns about customer trust, personal data and service reliability. He said passengers needed assurance that information submitted through digital booking platforms would be protected. Osanipin identified trust, reliability and responsive customer service as essential requirements for the success of digital mobility platforms. He also warned that launching new services was only the beginning, as operators would subsequently face the challenge of meeting growing customer expectations. “After we have launched today, the real work is going to start. A lot of customers will come in and demand this service. We have to be up to it,” he said. The Director-General urged GIGM to maintain service standards as it expanded, noting that technological innovation would have limited value without dependable customer experiences. Also speaking, the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Olufunso Adebiyi, represented by the Deputy Director of Road and Mass Transit, Usman Abubakar, expressed the ministry’s willingness to collaborate with private transport operators. “The Ministry of Transportation is willing and always has an open door for you to come and partner with us,” he said. Adebiyi described the company’s diversification into vehicle hire and digital mobility services as an example of private-sector innovation in transportation. He encouraged the company to sustain its expansion while developing services that would improve travel experiences for Nigerians.
